text:
maria: FYI customer (acct: x-123) is hitting invalid JSON when using structured_output=true. They get a parse error in our client: \"Invalid escape at position 82\" and the payload looks fine on their side. Happens for strings that end with a backslash or contain half surrogate pairs. Also noted a 500 once and a single token billed.

sam: Can you drop a minimal repro? model + api route + streaming flag?

maria: Minimal repro below (redacted):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer ****\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","structured_output":true,"input":"note: ends with backslash \\\\\\"}'
```
Server response: HTTP 500 and body: \"parse error: Unterminated string (invalid escape) at offset 128)\"

sam: Thanks. A couple quick checks: 1) is the customer using streaming=true at the client? 2) which SDK / proxy are they using?

maria: They use the JS SDK v1.2.3 with streaming=false. But they said they sometimes proxy through an internal gateway that does streaming transformations.

eng-ml-esc: This smells like chunk-boundary escape splitting. Even with streaming=false, some gateways will chunk or reserialize. Two failure modes we've seen: trailing single backslash (\\) that becomes an escape for the closing quote after any reserialization, and split surrogate pairs like \"\\ud83d\" (half of a UTF-16 surrogate) ending up emitting an invalid \"\\\\u\" escape.

eng-ml-esc: Can you repro locally by sending a payload where the model output contains a trailing backslash inside a JSON string? Example of the problematic output we saw in logs: 
```json
{
  \"summary\": \"Path to file: C:\\\\temp\\\\notes\\n\"\n}
```
Note how reserializers sometimes collapse or drop the final backslash and the JSON decoder then errors.

josh: Also customer complained about a spike in latency before the 500. Any chance a retry loop bubbled and created extra bills?

billing_bot: Failed requests that return 4xx/5xx are not billed for token consumption by default, but some partial-accept cases can incur a minimal charge. For account x-123 I see one charged request at 2026-02-22T14:03:11Z with status 200 and one failed 500 at 14:03:14Z.

claire: Workaround: ask customer to double-escape backslashes before sending (turn \\ into \\\\) or run a preflight JSON.stringify on the final model output on the gateway side. For half-surrogate issues, ensure full UTF-16 pairs are preserved (no substringing before re-encoding).

eng-ml-esc: We'll track as ENG-RUNTIME-482: serializer preserves trailing-backslash edge case. Could be in the structured-output post-processor that normalizes tokens into JSON. Please capture the raw request_id and the full request/response bodies (or base64 them) and attach to the ticket.

eng_bot: Trace created: trace_id=tr_2026_02_22_14_03_14_9a7f link=https://internal.redwood/trace/tr_2026_02_22_14_03_14_9a7f

maria: I'll add full raw payloads to the ticket and ask the customer to try the double-escape workaround.

sam: Quick temporary mitigation for JS SDK: run clientSideSanitizeEscapes(true) which will double-escape backslashes before sending. Not ideal but buys time.

maria: Thanks — escalating to eng-runtime and will follow up in the ticket. :thumbsup:

josh: :eyes:
